params.body:
## What went out repeatedly, and to whom

`VehicleObserver::updated` decided a vehicle was sold with

```php
filled($vehicle->sold_at) || filled($vehicle->sold_price) || $vehicle->sold == 1
```

That asks whether the fields are FILLED, not whether anything CHANGED, and those three fields stay filled forever. So every later save of a sold vehicle took the sold branch again: it dispatched `sold` to every receiver of the dealer plus every receiver without a dealer, and cleared `send_to_modix` again with a second quiet save. Eleven receivers are configured today (three global: Doorlinken Voorraad, `admin.yourdailydrive.com`, `backend.flexlease.rent`; eight for Okasie, one per dealer), so a dealer who reopened a sold vehicle and saved it rang eleven partners. Reopening it ten times rang them ten times each.

## Why it reached Hexon as a repeated delete

The per-receiver flags do not choose who is rung, only what they are told (R S2-10.6). Doorlinken Voorraad, the system behind Hexon, has `sold` switched off, so `WebhookHelper::resolveWebhookType` translates a sale into `delete` for that receiver. A repeat therefore arrived there as a `delete` for an object Hexon had already removed, which is exactly what an API answers with an error code. The dealer heard about it from Hexon; nothing showed on our side, because a 4xx/5xx is written to `webhook_logs` as if it had been accepted (finding X-99).

## The transition signal, and why this one

The predicate itself is unchanged; it is now asked twice, once on the values as they stand after the save and once on `getOriginal(...)` of the same three fields. The branch runs its outbound work only when the vehicle counts as sold now and did not before.

`isDirty('sold')` was the obvious candidate and is not the right one, on two counts.

- It is true in both directions. The partner API can mark a vehicle unsold again (`VehicleApiController::markAsSold` with `sold` false, which writes `sold => 0, sold_at => null, sold_price => null`), and `isDirty('sold')` would have sent `sold` on that move too.
- It is keyed on one column. Every path that sells a vehicle today does write `sold` alongside `sold_at` and `sold_price`, and I checked each of them: the sheet through `OwnStockController::update_sold` and `OwnStockList::markSold`, the buy-over in `App\Http\Helpers\Vehicle` (which writes `sold`, `sold_at`, `sold_price`, `on_stock`, `available_on_stocklist` and `send_to_modix` in one update), the order in `OrderController`, and the partner API through `markAsSold`. The console commands do not mark vehicles sold; `stocklist:forceUpdateWebhooks` reads `sold` and calls the inline path directly, untouched by this change. But a path that only stamped `sold_at` would have gone silent under `isDirty('sold')`, and going silent about a sale is worse than the defect being fixed. Comparing the whole condition keeps every such path at exactly one message.

A vehicle that is already sold still enters the same branch and does nothing there, rather than falling through to the branches below it. That is deliberate: what hangs further down (Nederland Mobiel, the `update` webhook, the export mail) was never reachable for a sold vehicle and must not open up now.

The second, quiet save is `saveQuietly()`, so it fires no model events and re-triggers nothing. On a later save of a sold vehicle it does not run at all. The older rule in `Vehicle::booted` that clears the same flag inside the same UPDATE is keyed on `getOriginal('sold') == 0 && $model->sold == 1`, the same transition, so the two still agree: on the sale both clear the flag, and on every later save neither does. `test_the_modix_rule_and_the_observer_agree_on_clearing_the_flag` now asserts that second half as well.

## Characterization tests

- `test_every_later_save_of_a_sold_vehicle_rings_sold_again` encoded the defect and is replaced by `test_a_later_save_of_a_sold_vehicle_rings_nothing`: the sale rings once, and three further saves ring nobody. That is the assertion that would have caught this.
- `test_the_sale_rings_once_whichever_shape_the_update_has` is new: the buy-over shape (sold plus the stock flags plus `send_to_modix => 0` in one update) rings exactly once, and a save that only stamps `sold_at` rings once as well, after which the matching `sold`/`sold_price` write rings nothing.
- `test_marking_a_vehicle_unsold_does_not_ring_sold` is new: the API's reverse move rings nothing.
- `test_the_modix_rule_and_the_observer_agree_on_clearing_the_flag` gained the later-save half.
- The class docblock was adjusted on the one line that described the sold branch.

Rule R S2-10.3 already said "eenmalig" as the intent; it now says so explicitly and names the transition, so rule and code agree. X-97 moves to the resolved table of `90-x-bevindingen.md` with what was done, as X-95 and X-96 were moved, and the rule keeps its `@rule S2-10.3` tag and its tests. `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` were regenerated (`bin/rules-coverage --write`, `bin/rules-page`); the coverage counts are unchanged, so only the HTML moved.

## Deliberately untouched

X-98 (the identifiers are obfuscated with `(id * 3) + 5`, not encrypted) and X-99 (a 4xx/5xx is logged as if it had been accepted, and nothing retries) are recorded and stay as they are. The publisher seam (O-22 to O-25) is not refactored. The cutover is tomorrow; this is one change with its tests.

## Tests

`vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='VehiclePublishing|Webhook|Observer|Vehicle|Outbound|RulesCoverage'`: 193 tests, 793 assertions, 1 skipped, no failures. The full suite: 705 tests, 2916 assertions, 1 skipped, the only failure being `BuildStampTest` (a worktree artifact: `.git` is a file there, not a directory).
params.title: A sold vehicle rings the partners once, not on every save
